body.prompt: Review the correctness risk of speculative decoding with a target verifier. Give concise invariants for preserving greedy output.
Explain why a persistent exact token continuation cache can accelerate repeated local code-completion requests without changing target output.
List the minimal tests that prove cancellation cannot teach a persistent continuation cache.
Describe when a maximum speculative draft length should be reduced for correctness rather than tuned for throughput.
Analyze the tradeoff between an SSD-backed exact continuation cache and an in-memory ngram cache for repeated developer requests.
What telemetry should distinguish persistent cache hits, current-context proposals, misses, and accepted speculative tokens?
Explain a bounded recovery design for an append-only local cache with records, manifests, and a hot index.
Give a concise checklist for testing a cache compaction crash boundary.
Review a local HTTP capture proxy that records only visible request bodies before forwarding them to a model server. What privacy constraints matter?
Explain why a request-capture ledger should use a hash chain and fsync before forwarding.
How should an HTTP proxy preserve SSE first-token latency while relaying a streaming model response?
What should happen to an upstream streaming response when the downstream client disconnects?
Describe a fair three-arm local benchmark comparing baseline decoding, upstream ngram speculation, and persistent exact speculation.
Why must a benchmark preserve every timeout, miss, and output mismatch instead of removing outliers?
Explain clustered bootstrap confidence intervals for paired request-family latency measurements.
Define a conservative no-persistent-hit overhead population for a cache benchmark.
Review a C++ design that bounds disk bytes, index RAM, lookup probes, and bytes read for a local persistent cache.
Explain why a cache writer lock and private file permissions matter on a single-user local model server.
Give a compact algorithm for checking an exact token suffix against a persisted continuation record.
What is a safe policy when a persistent cache record is corrupt or identity-incompatible?
Explain why a semantic edit to a code prompt often fails to produce an exact persistent continuation-cache hit.
Describe the difference between exact-reuse capability evidence and representative development-workload evidence.
What evidence is needed before enabling a persistent speculative cache by default?
Explain why a positive point estimate is insufficient when a confidence lower bound misses the preregistered threshold.
Review the performance implications of copying prompt tokens and repeatedly hashing suffixes during speculative cache lookup.
Suggest a safe way to reduce per-hit disk open and allocation overhead while preserving checksum verification.
Explain why rejected speculative drafts can hurt end-to-end latency even when lookup time is small.
What does it mean when persistent hits are absent on a naturalistic development stream?
Summarize a release checklist for a local experimental persistent speculative cache integrated into a model server.
Describe how to separate product correctness receipts from performance qualification receipts.
Explain why a capture workload must be sealed before benchmark arms are launched.
What is the narrowest honest claim after a passing project-local development benchmark?
